resources.name: Lut Presets
resources.author: ov-studio
resources.tagline: A curated collection of color grading LUT presets
resources.description:
Lut is a curated pack of 63 color grading presets, organized into
five collections: Cinematic, Moody, Portrait, ColorBoost, and
Lutify — covering everything from film-inspired tones to punchy
color boosts and natural skin-tone shaping.

Apply, swap, or reset LUTs on the fly through simple exported APIs,
making it easy to wire up your own menu or let other resources control grading directly.

**Exports:**
• `util.export.call("lut_presets", "get_list")` - returns all preset paths
• `util.export.call("lut_presets", "get_lut")` - returns active preset index, or false
• `util.export.call("lut_presets", "set_lut", index)` - applies preset by index
• `util.export.call("lut_presets", "reset_lut")` - clears the active LUT

**Commands:**
• `/lut <index>` - applies preset by index from the console

resources.name: Profiler
resources.author: ov-studio
resources.tagline: Live FPS, memory, native and entity stats overlay
resources.description:
Profiler is an in-game overlay that tracks live client performance
and debug stats: FPS, memory usage, per-native timings, and
per-entity-type counts (peds, vehicles, objects, and so on).

Native/entity stats are auto-registered for every entity type the
engine exposes, so new types are picked up automatically with no
extra configuration. Each panel is draggable, resizable, and
brings itself to front on click, so you can arrange the overlay
however suits your workflow.

Perfect for spotting frame drops, memory leaks, and entity/native
bloat while developing or debugging live.

**Commands:**
• `/profiler` - toggles the profiler overlay on/off

resources.name: Runcode
resources.author: ov-studio
resources.tagline: Execute Lua code directly from the console
resources.description:
Runcode is a lightweight runtime code executor that works on both
the client and the server.

Compile and execute arbitrary Lua on the fly directly from the
console — no need to reload scripts or restart. Both expressions
and statements are supported, and results (or errors) are printed
straight back to you, formatted and easy to read.

Perfect for quick debugging, prototyping, and live tweaks, whether
you're working client-side or server-side.

**Commands:**
• `/run <code>` - compiles and executes Lua code on the fly

resources.name: Skycycle
resources.author: ov-studio
resources.tagline: Dynamic volumetric sky, weather and day/night cycle
resources.description:
Skycycle is a complete dynamic sky for Vital.sandbox: a server-synced
day/night cycle with a physically inspired sun and moon, volumetric
clouds, stars, god rays, sun bloom and fourteen weather presets.

Rain and snow are real GPU particles that collide with the level, so
nothing falls indoors. Every raindrop that lands splashes and rings a
ripple exactly where it hits, ground gets wet and forms puddles, and
snow settles on up-facing surfaces and melts again. Lightning, fog,
wind and the scene light and ambient follow the weather.

Needs an engine with GPU particle collision, `particle:set_layer` and
HDR rendertargets. Everything tunable lives in `config.lua`.

**Credits:**
• Moon texture: derived from NASA's CGI Moon Kit "lroc_color_poles" (2019), downsampled to 2048x1024 - NASA/GSFC/Scientific Visualization Studio, LRO/LOLA, LROC/ASU, visualizations by Ernie Wright - https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/4720/

**Exports (server):**
• `util.export.call("skycycle", "set_time", hour)` - sets the hour (0-24)
• `util.export.call("skycycle", "set_weather", name)` - changes the weather
• `util.export.call("skycycle", "set_timescale", scale)` - 1 = normal, 0 = freeze
• `util.export.call("skycycle", "get_time")` - returns the current hour

**Exports (client):**
• `set_rain`, `set_snow`, `set_fog`, `set_lightning`, `set_wind`, `set_wind_dir`
• `set_snow_cover`, `set_sun_size`, `set_moon_size`, `set_moon_phase`, `get_moon_phase`
• `get_time`, `get_weather`, `flash`, `toggle`

**Commands:**
• `/time <hour | HH:MM>` - sets the time of day
• `/weather <name>` - clear, partly, cloudy, overcast, storm, hazy, drizzle, rain, thunder, snow, blizzard, fog, sandstorm, smog
• `/timescale <n>` - 1 = normal, 0 = freeze, 60 = fast
• `/sky_rain`, `/sky_snow`, `/sky_fog`, `/sky_lightning <0-1 | auto>` - intensity while the weather has it
• `/sky_wind <0-6 | auto>` and `/sky_winddir <degrees>` - wind strength and direction
• `/snow_cover <0-1 | auto>` - snow on surfaces
• `/sky_quality <low|medium|high|ultra>` - cloud quality
• `/sky_clouds`, `/sky_precip`, `/sky_splash`, `/sky_glow`, `/sky_godrays`, `/sky_toggle [on|off]`
• `/sun_size <deg>`, `/moon_size <deg>`, `/moon_phase <name | 0-1 | auto>`
